Trail Physics · Unit 4: Energy & Momentum · Module 10

Energy and Gravitation

Kinetic, gravitational and elastic potential energy, conservation of mechanical energy, and Newton’s law of gravitation.

Lesson coming

The question

Where does your speed come from when you drop into a descent?

The physics

  • Work
  • Kinetic energy
  • Gravitational potential energy
  • Elastic potential energy
  • Conservation of mechanical energy
  • Conservative forces
  • Gravitation

The math

  • KE = ½mv²
  • PE = mgh
  • PE_spring = ½kx²
  • KE₁ + PE₁ = KE₂ + PE₂ (no losses)
  • F = Gm₁m₂ / r²

Learning objectives

  • Calculate kinetic energy
  • Calculate gravitational potential energy
  • Use conservation of mechanical energy to predict speed after a descent
  • Calculate the energy stored in a compressed spring
  • Account for energy lost to friction and other non-conservative forces
  • Describe Newton’s law of gravitation and gravitational fields

Helps to know first: Newton’s Laws of Motion.

The mountain biking connection

At the top of a trail a rider has height; at the bottom, speed. Gravitational potential energy turns into kinetic energy, and some of it into heat and sound along the way.
